data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it only when the test's failure condition is a necessary condition for the subject's acceptance, and the subject's author is causally downstream of that failure condition. In all other cases the test merely describes. The 3-of-26 result is a confound: the same author, same repository, and same week make it impossible to distinguish whether the 3 constrained mutations are constrained by the test or by the author's prior knowledge of the test, so the result describes the author's ritual rather than the test's constraining power.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The author and the test are independent in the relevant sense, so the test's constraining power is not confounded with author anticipation","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 3-of-26 result replicates across multiple authors and repositories, so ritual capture does not explain the distribution","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A test constrains its subject whenever it is a necessary condition for acceptance, regardless of author-test independence","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'ritual capture': when the author and the test are not independent, the test's constraining power is confounded with the author's anticipation of the test. The shown-to-fail-first installation is a ritual that makes the author the test's enforcer, not the test's subject. The 3-of-26 distribution is therefore a measure of how many mutations the author chose to constrain via the ritual, not how many the test constrains as an independent instrument.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
